Jabneel
JAB-nee-el
proper noun
Hebrew Yavne’el, “God causeth to build” or “God will build,” the name of two border towns.

📖 Biblical Definition

Jabneel was the name of two towns that marked the borders of the tribal inheritances. One lay on the boundary of Judah toward the sea, between the mountain of Baalah and the great sea, in the list of Judah’s coastal landmarks (Josh 15:11); this town was later known as Jabneh or Jamnia. The other Jabneel was a border town of Naphtali in the north, named among the fenced cities of that tribe near the sea of Chinnereth (Josh 19:33). The name itself is a confession of faith woven into the map of the land: “God causeth to build,” or “God will build.” Every boundary stone and border town of Israel was set by the hand of the LORD who divided the inheritance to the tribes by lot, so that the very names of the towns bore witness to the God who planted His people in the land. Jabneel, small and little mentioned, stands among the borders as a quiet reminder that it is God who builds the house and the city; except the LORD build it, they labour in vain that build it (Ps 127:1). The bounds of Israel were not the work of men’s ambition but the gift and building of God.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A border town, by one of two sites, whose name confesses that God builds; on the bounds of Judah and of Naphtali.

expand to see more

JABNEEL, the name of two border towns in the tribal inheritances.

One marked the border of Judah toward the sea, later called Jabneh (Josh 15:11).

The other was a fenced city on the border of Naphtali (Josh 19:33).

Its name signifies “God causeth to build” or “God will build.”

It stands among the boundary marks of the land divided by lot.

📖 Key Scripture

Josh 15:11 — "And the border went out unto the side of Ekron northward: and the border was drawn to Shicron, and passed along to mount Baalah, and went out unto Jabneel; and the goings out of the border were at the sea."

Josh 19:33 — "And their coast was from Heleph, from Allon to Zaanannim, and Adami, Nekeb, and Jabneel, unto Lakum; and the outgoings thereof were at Jordan:"

Ps 127:1 — "Except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the LORD keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain."

Josh 14:5 — "As the LORD commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did, and they divided the land."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A place-name, not a doctrine in dispute; its lesson is that God Himself builds the house and the city of His people.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is sealed in the name: “God will build.” The borders of Israel were not drawn by the cunning of men but apportioned by the LORD through the lot, so that the very towns confessed His hand. Except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it; the prosperity of a people, a family, or a church is the gift of God, not the achievement of human strength.

Jabneel, little remembered, also teaches that no part of God’s ordering is too small for His care. He numbered the border stones and named the obscure towns of His people. The same God who builds the unnamed places builds the lives of the humblest of His saints, whose names are written in heaven though forgotten on earth.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name joins a verb “to build” with El, “God,” confessing that God is the builder.

expand to see more

Jabneel — Hebrew Yavne’el, “God causeth to build.”

The element El (“God”) closes many Hebrew names.

The verb-root banah means to build or establish.

One Jabneel lay in Judah, another in Naphtali.

The border-town’s name confesses the God who builds His people’s house.

Usage

"Like Jabneel, every house and city of God’s people is built by His hand, not by human strength."

"Jabneel teaches that except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it."

"The obscure border-town confesses by its very name the God who orders even the smallest things."
